title: RFQ restart and replay: a crashed sender resumes the exact signed packet (never signs a second turn), and a replayed packet is recognised as a duplicate with no state change

clauses.DACS-3 §8.3.3 (channel message envelope): sequence: number — monotonic per channel, starts at 1.
clauses.DACS-3 §8.12 (replay of offers across se: The channel message envelope includes channelId and sequence (per-channel monotonic). Given CH-6, an offer replayed into a different channel fails signature verification because the channelId differs; replayed in the same channel it duplicates a sequence number and is rejected.
clauses.DACS-3 §8.2 CH-6 (per-session channelId: The substrate MUST derive a per-session-unique channelId, and an orchestrator MUST reject a session that reuses a channelId from a prior session.

spec.honestScope: The durable RFQ lifecycle (dacs-sdk src/negotiate/durableRfqLifecycle{,StoreFs}.ts) is an SDK-side surface. Identity, Vet and Listing verification are synthetic fixture authority here (disposition: verified is asserted, not verified); transport is a local file spool, not the Demos encrypted wire; the clock is fixed. What these vectors pin is the restart/replay discipline the quoted clauses require of any conforming negotiation endpoint: a restarted sender reconciles its durable outbox and reuses the exact signed packet rather than signing a new turn, and a same-channel replayed packet is rejected as a duplicate with revision, transcript and sequence unchanged.

derivation: Expected checkpoints are derived from the quoted clauses: monotonic per-channel sequence means re-sending after an uncertain publish must reuse the already-signed sequence (one packet, no second signature), and a receiver seeing an already-processed sequence must report a duplicate without state change. Each lifecycle action runs in a fresh OS process over the durable store, so every expectation is a restart-survival claim.
fixtures: Two local roles (buyer, seller) with fresh Ed25519 keys per run; negotiable listing bandCenter 10 USDC ±20%; local file-spool transport; fixed synthetic clock; no network, no testnet, no payment, no Demos wire signatures.

vectors.name: crash-after-durable-publish-resumes-exact-packet
vectors.cite: DACS-3 §8.3.3: sequence is monotonic per channel — a sender that crashed after durably publishing but before acknowledgement MUST resume the same signed packet, never sign a fresh turn for the same sequence
vectors.scenario: buyer sends the opening offer with an injected crash (exit 86) after the durable spool write, before acknowledgement; a fresh buyer process then resumes the outbox

vectors.name: same-packet-replay-is-duplicate-no-state-change
vectors.cite: DACS-3 §8.12: replayed in the same channel it duplicates a sequence number and is rejected — observable as a duplicate verdict with revision and transcript unchanged
vectors.scenario: a fresh seller process replays the exact offer packet it has already processed

vectors.name: full-negotiation-exact-transcript-no-duplicates
vectors.cite: DACS-3 §8.3.3 monotonic sequence + §8.12: after offer, counter and accept (each action in a fresh process), both roles hold exactly three turns, identical transcripts, and one identical dual-signed agreement at the accepted price
vectors.scenario: seller counters at 9.5, buyer accepts, both roles finalize the agreement; every action is a fresh OS process over the durable stores
